prerequisites: Knowledge of calculus as learnt during the first year of engineering studies: complex numbers, limits, derivatives, integrals, study of functions.
Calculation of areas and volumes of simple shapes.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacity of application of principles of basic physics, especially classical mechanics (kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid body) and electromagnetism (electric force, electric field, magnetic induction field, electric currents, Maxwell's equations in integral form) in vacuum.
Through lectures students learn the basic principles of physics, with particular emphasis on classical mechanics and electromagnetism in vacuum.

Through exercises and numerical problems, the student is able to apply the acquired knowledge for predicting physical phenomena inherent in classical physics, mechanics and electromagnetism in vacuum.
Through exercises and self study the student is able to understand, critically discuss and present the results obtained and the approximations made.

The preparation for the written exam allows the student to develop the ability to expose risults correctly, effectively and concisely, to express the concepts learned with appropriate language and to hold a discussion about the topics covered.
The activities described allow the students to acquire the methodological tools to continue their studies and to be able to arrange their own upgrade.

syllabus_topics: Linear motion: equations of motion, definitions of velocity and acceleration
Harmonic motion (Definition of vectors, . operations with vectors
Motion in two and three dimensions
Force, relation between force and motion
Kinetic energy and work: theorem of kinetic energy
Potential energy, conservative forces, determination of potential energy
Second law of Newton for rotation
II law of Newton in angular form
Angular momentum for rotation around an axis
IV Maxwell equation in the non stationary case: displacement current
teaching_methods: Lectures also assisted with audiovisual tools
assessment_rules: The written examination consists of a calculation part (2 problems) and a theory part (5 open questions). A maximum of 15 points is assigned for each problem and 6 points for each theory question. The test is passed if at least 18 points are obtained in both parts. The final vote is the average between the scores of the two parts. Scores are assigned based on formal correctness and completeness (80%) and technical language and clarity (20%).
